problems.quote: Random assignment allocated 73 participants to the treatment group and 32 to the control group.
problems.note: Random assignment is explicit, but the paper does not establish a laboratory, online-panel, or ordinary-work/coursework setting. The current codebook expressly provides unstated_rct for a randomized experiment whose setting is not stated, and the extraction specification permits that code. Replace null with unstated_rct. The printed field here gives the required codebook classification, not a literal term from the paper. Update the associated open_items and notes that incorrectly say no permitted design_class can be confirmed.

summary: Checked all five estimates against the PDF and read the complete 470-line markdown conversion through the final reference; the 16-page paper has no appendix. All recorded estimate statistics match the cited prose on PDF pp. 9-10 and belong to the specified outcome and persona-versus-standard contrast. The outcome coding, directions, units, AI availability, timing, comparison type, within-person status, and se_basis are supported. Study-level randomized and analyzed totals match PDF pp. 4-5. Leaving analysis counts null is justified by the unresolved arm-count conflict and absence of unambiguous outcome-specific counts: the results prose gives 69 persona and 32 control logs, whereas Figure 6 labels its arms 70 and 31. Both supplied script warnings are false negatives from the PDF text layer. Direct in-memory inspection of the embedded Figure 6 on PDF p. 10 confirms the literal label Welch p above both the middle all-participant comparison and the right cross-condition nearest comparison, supporting their recorded t-test types. No additional eligible output outcome or full-sample contrast was found; self-reports, engagement measures, trait/subgroup results, and exploratory correlations are appropriately excluded. The sole identified error is the missing unstated_rct design code in the study record.
